q1: SELECT A.PROJECT_ID, ROUND(AVG(B.EXPERIENCE_YEARS), 2) AS AVERAGE_YEARS FROM PROJECT AS A INNER JOIN EMPLOYEE AS B ON A.EMPLOYEE_ID = B.EMPLOYEE_ID GROUP BY A.PROJECT_ID
q2: SELECT P.PROJECT_ID, ROUND(AVG(EXPERIENCE_YEARS),2) AS AVERAGE_YEARS FROM PROJECT P JOIN EMPLOYEE E ON P.EMPLOYEE_ID=E.EMPLOYEE_ID GROUP BY 1
q1_prompt_sql: SELECT A.PROJECT_ID, ROUND(AVG(B.EXPERIENCE_YEARS), 2) AS AVERAGE_YEARS FROM PROJECT AS A INNER JOIN EMPLOYEE AS B ON A.EMPLOYEE_ID = B.EMPLOYEE_ID GROUP BY A.PROJECT_ID
q2_prompt_sql: SELECT P.PROJECT_ID, ROUND(AVG(EXPERIENCE_YEARS),2) AS AVERAGE_YEARS FROM PROJECT P JOIN EMPLOYEE E ON P.EMPLOYEE_ID=E.EMPLOYEE_ID GROUP BY 1
explanation: Both queries aim to calculate the average years of experience for employees associated with each project. They use the same JOIN condition, GROUP BY clause, and the same AVG function to achieve this. The only difference is the aliasing of the tables and the use of the GROUP BY 1 shorthand in the second query, which is equivalent to GROUP BY PROJECT_ID.
